# peaks: `PeaksOutput`

The `data` payload of `openreadout analyze peaks FILE --json` (`--rt T --window W`, `--integrate A-B`, `--targets LIST.csv`), inside the [envelope](envelope.md).

Output of `analyze peaks`.

JSON Schema: [`docs/schema/peaks.schema.json`](https://github.com/openreadout/openreadout/blob/main/docs/schema/peaks.schema.json) · also printed by `openreadout self schema peaks`.

## Fields

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | The input file. |
| `format` | `string` | yes | Format id of the input file. |
| `chromatograms` | array of [`ChromatogramPeaks`](#chromatogrampeaks) | yes | One entry per analysed chromatogram. |
| `compounds` | array of [`CompoundResult`](#compoundresult) |  | One row per compound of the compound list. |
| `spectra` | array of [`SpectrumBands`](#spectrumbands) |  | Spectra (traces whose axis is not time: wavenumber, wavelength, ppm, …): bands and integrated regions, one entry per analysed spectrum. |
| `outputs` | array of `string` |  | Files written (`-o`, `--plot`). |
| `notes` | array of `string` |  | Anything the caller should know. |

### ChromatogramPeaks

| `kind` | `string` | yes | `tic`, `bpc`, `xic`, `srm` or `trace`. |

| `mz` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | XIC m/z. |

### PeakMethod

The method that produced a peak table, with every parameter actually used.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `smoothing` | `string` | yes | `savitzky_golay_quadratic` or `none`. |
| `smooth_window_points` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Smoothing window in points (1 = none). |
| `smooth_auto` | `boolean` | yes | True when the window was chosen automatically. |
| `characteristic_width_points` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Median width at half height of the most prominent maxima, points (drives the automatic smoothing and baseline windows). |
| `noise` | `number` (double) | yes | Noise σ, signal units. |
| `noise_method` | `string` | yes | `segment_rms`, `segment_rms_nonzero`, `mad_first_difference`, `user` or `none`. |
| `min_snr` | `number` (double) | yes | Detection threshold, S/N. |
| `min_height` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Detection threshold, signal units. |
| `min_width_min` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Smallest width at half height, minutes. |
| `min_points` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Fewest samples per peak. |
| `baseline` | `string` | yes | `drop`, `valley` or `tangent`. |
| `skim_ratio` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | `tangent` skim ratio. |
| `baseline_window_points` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Window of the running baseline, points. |
| `slope_noise` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | `auto`: noise of the smoothed signal's derivative, signal units per minute (flanks end below [`AUTO_END_SLOPE_NOISE`] times it). |
| `look_ahead_points` | `integer` (uint32) or `null` |  | `auto`: how far a flat stretch must go on without a valley to end a peak, points. |
| `rt_range_min` | array of 2 × `number` (double) or `null` |  | Retention-time range searched, minutes. |
| `integration` | `string` | yes | `trapezoid`. |
| `area_time_unit` | `string` | yes | Time unit of `area`: `min` or `s`. |
| `points` | `integer` (uint64) | yes | Samples analysed. |

### Peak

One integrated peak (a flat record: one row of a peak table).

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | 1-based peak number in retention-time order. |
| `rt_min` | `number` (double) | yes | Retention time of the apex, minutes. |
| `start_min` | `number` (double) | yes | Peak start (integration start), minutes. |
| `end_min` | `number` (double) | yes | Peak end (integration end), minutes. |
| `height` | `number` (double) | yes | Height of the apex above the baseline, signal units. |
| `area` | `number` (double) | yes | Area above the baseline between start and end, signal units × `area_time_unit`. |
| `area_percent` | `number` (double) | yes | Share of the summed area of all peaks in the table, %. |
| `width_half_min` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Width at half height, minutes (absent when the signal does not fall to half height before a drop line). |
| `width_10pct_min` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Width at 10 % height, minutes. |
| `width_5pct_min` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Width at 5 % height, minutes. |
| `width_base_min` | `number` (double) | yes | End − start, minutes. |
| `tailing_factor` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | USP tailing factor `W₀.₀₅ / 2f` (f: apex to the leading edge at 5 % height). |
| `asymmetry_factor` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Asymmetry factor `b/a` at 10 % height (a: leading half-width, b: trailing half-width). |
| `plates` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Theoretical plates, half-height method `5.54 (t_R / W½)²` (t_R from time zero). |
| `resolution` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Resolution to the previous peak, `1.18 (t₂ − t₁) / (W½₁ + W½₂)`. |
| `snr` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Height / noise σ (absent when the noise is 0). |
| `points` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Samples from start to end. |
| `baseline_code` | `string` | yes | How each end meets the baseline: `B` baseline, `V` valley (drop line), `T` tangent skim, `M` manual (given boundaries); e.g. `BB`, `BV`, `VB`, `TT`. |
| `baseline_start` | `number` (double) | yes | Baseline value at the start, signal units. |
| `baseline_end` | `number` (double) | yes | Baseline value at the end, signal units. |
| `baseline_reason` | `string` or `null` |  | `auto` baseline: why the baseline was drawn this way — `sloped_background` (an end was placed where the peak meets a sloped or drifting background), `drop_line` (fused with a neighbour: common baseline, vertical drop line at the valley), `baseline_penetration` (split from a neighbour where the signal dips below their common baseline), `isolated` (both ends on the baseline). The first that applies. |

### Band

One detected band.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | 1-based band number in order of increasing x. |
| `x` | `number` (double) | yes | Apex position (vertex of the parabola through the three highest smoothed points), axis units. |

| `baseline_end` | `number` (double) | yes | Baseline at the end, signal units. |

### Region

One integrated region of a spectrum.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | 1-based region number in request order. |
| `from` | `number` (double) | yes | Lower end asked for, axis units. |
| `to` | `number` (double) | yes | Upper end asked for, axis units. |
| `x_first` | `number` (double) | yes | Axis value of the first sample used. |
| `x_last` | `number` (double) | yes | Axis value of the last sample used. |
| `points` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Samples used. |
| `baseline` | `string` | yes | `linear` or `none`. |
| `baseline_start` | `number` (double) | yes | Baseline at `x_first`, signal units. |
| `baseline_end` | `number` (double) | yes | Baseline at `x_last`, signal units. |
| `area` | `number` (double) | yes | Trapezoidal integral of (signal − baseline), signal units × axis units. |
| `area_no_baseline` | `number` (double) | yes | Trapezoidal integral of the signal itself. |
| `max_x` | `number` (double) | yes | Axis value of the region maximum (the sample of largest signal − baseline; of largest baseline − signal when bands are minima). |
| `max_height` | `number` (double) | yes | Height of the maximum above the baseline (depth below it when bands are minima). |
| `max_value` | `number` (double) | yes | Signal at the maximum. |
| `centroid` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | (signal − baseline)-weighted mean axis value (absent when that integral is not positive). |
| `peaks` | array of `integer` (uint32) |  | Numbers of the detected bands whose apex lies in the region. |
| `peaks_area` | `number` (double) | yes | Summed area of those bands (each above its own detection baseline). |
